description: Snapshot of Arrival task rules and their source links; no live eligibility decisions.

tasks.title: Confirm your entry route
tasks.body: Check the entry requirements for your passport nationality and travel purpose with the official portal and airline. Your current country of residence alone does not establish visa eligibility. Confirm passport validity and any required permit before booking.

tasks.title: Start your job search before travelling
tasks.body: Prepare a targeted CV and use employer career pages, LinkedIn, Bayt and GulfTalent. Contact recruiters relevant to your industry and request an online meeting or an appointment; interviews and placements are not guaranteed. Verify offers before paying any intermediary.

tasks.title: Prepare the documents your route needs
tasks.body: Request the authority’s current checklist for passports, photos, qualifications, company papers or family certificates. Confirm attestation and translation requirements for each document; not every foreign-issued document follows the same process.

tasks.title: Arrange your flight and airport transfer
tasks.body: Include Etihad when comparing flights to Abu Dhabi. Check entry requirements, baggage, flexible fares and cancellation terms. Keep your temporary accommodation address and arrival documents handy; arrange a licensed airport transfer.

tasks.title: Start with a flexible temporary home
tasks.body: Compare hotel apartments, serviced apartments and suitable holiday-home listings before signing a long lease. Check total cost, cancellation, kitchen/laundry facilities, listing permissions and the commute. For a family, check room capacity and nearby everyday services.

tasks.title: Coordinate residence, medical and Emirates ID
tasks.body: Follow your sponsor or authority’s sequence. Residence applicants aged 18 and over generally need medical fitness screening. Use an approved centre, complete required Emirates ID application/biometrics and track residence processing. Timelines depend on the route and appointments.

tasks.title: Arrange your health insurance
tasks.body: Check Abu Dhabi health insurance requirements and who must arrange and pay for coverage. Compare networks, exclusions, waiting periods and pre-existing-condition cover. Residence medical screening is separate from insurance; include dependants and elderly parents in the insurance discussion.

tasks.title: Connect your phone and government services
tasks.body: Arrange a SIM with a licensed provider, checking the identification requirements. Set up UAE PASS where eligible and use TAMM and ICP for the services relevant to your route. Some services require their own apps even though this planner works in the browser.

tasks.title: Get around with taxis and Hafilat buses
tasks.body: Use Abu Dhabi Taxi and check live availability and fares with ride providers. Abu Dhabi public buses use Hafilat cards; consult Abu Dhabi Mobility for card and route details. Compare your likely commute before deciding on a car.

tasks.title: Prepare for personal and business banking
tasks.body: Ask the selected bank for its current account requirements, identity/residence evidence and any income or address records. Business accounts need a separate corporate and beneficial-owner file. Approval, minimum balances and timelines depend on the bank.

tasks.title: Decide where to live after exploring
tasks.body: Compare areas such as Al Reem, Yas, Saadiyat and Al Raha against your commute, household needs and budget. Inspect homes, verify agents and review payment terms. For a long-term lease, confirm Tawtheeq registration and utility requirements; for a purchase, obtain legal and financial due diligence.

tasks.title: Set up everyday services and local connections
tasks.body: Check food and shopping delivery coverage at your address. Browse professional and community events, arrange introductions and find a regular activity. Confirm organisers’ current dates and registration requirements.

tasks.title: Track costs, renewals and next steps
tasks.body: Use the budget worksheet to enter confirmed quotes for travel, temporary housing, permits, insurance, deposits and living costs. Note which costs the employer covers. Add residence, ID, policy, licence and lease expiry dates to your calendar; residence is renewable, not a promise of permanent status.

tasks.title: Connect your phone and government services
tasks.body: Arrange a SIM with a licensed provider, checking the identification requirements. Set up UAE PASS where eligible and use TAMM and ICP for the services relevant to your route. Some services require their own apps even though this planner works in the browser.

tasks.title: Get around with taxis and Hafilat buses
tasks.body: Use Abu Dhabi Taxi and check live availability and fares with ride providers. Abu Dhabi public buses use Hafilat cards; consult Abu Dhabi Mobility for card and route details. Compare your likely commute before deciding on a car.

tasks.title: Plan each family member’s residence and work
tasks.body: Check dependent sponsorship eligibility and document requirements separately. If your partner will work online or start a business, confirm the necessary authorisation rather than assuming dependent residence covers it. Each person may need their own tailored route.

tasks.title: Check your parents’ residence and care needs
tasks.body: Ask ICP about the applicable parent sponsorship route, income/accommodation evidence and supporting documents. Compare age-specific insurance and care needs before travel. Do not assume parents have the same rules as a spouse or child.

tasks.title: Prepare for personal and business banking
tasks.body: Ask the selected bank for its current account requirements, identity/residence evidence and any income or address records. Business accounts need a separate corporate and beneficial-owner file. Approval, minimum balances and timelines depend on the bank.

tasks.title: Plan wealth transfers and estate arrangements
tasks.body: Discuss account opening, transfer limits and source-of-funds evidence with the receiving bank before moving funds. Obtain advice on your previous country’s tax residence, UAE obligations and succession planning. For wills or a family office, use qualified legal and tax advisers and confirm the applicable framework.

tasks.title: Check business, tax and recordkeeping obligations
tasks.body: Review corporate tax, VAT and filing obligations for the actual activity and entity. Free-zone treatment is conditional. Separate personal investment from business activity, and ask an adviser about cross-border tax residence. Keep sourced records rather than relying on a blanket “tax-free” claim.

tasks.title: Decide where to live after exploring
tasks.body: Compare areas such as Al Reem, Yas, Saadiyat and Al Raha against your commute, household needs and budget. Inspect homes, verify agents and review payment terms. For a long-term lease, confirm Tawtheeq registration and utility requirements; for a purchase, obtain legal and financial due diligence.

tasks.title: Explore nursery or school options
tasks.body: Use the children’s ages to decide whether nursery, kindergarten or school planning is relevant. Check admission ages, places, fees, documents, term dates and transport with schools and the Abu Dhabi education authority before committing.

tasks.title: Hire household support through authorised channels
tasks.body: Use a licensed domestic-worker recruitment route. Confirm the contract, sponsorship, insurance, wages and employer obligations through MOHRE before hiring.

tasks.title: Set up everyday services and local connections
tasks.body: Check food and shopping delivery coverage at your address. Browse professional and community events, arrange introductions and find a regular activity. Confirm organisers’ current dates and registration requirements.

tasks.title: Track costs, renewals and next steps
tasks.body: Use the budget worksheet to enter confirmed quotes for travel, temporary housing, permits, insurance, deposits and living costs. Note which costs the employer covers. Add residence, ID, policy, licence and lease expiry dates to your calendar; residence is renewable, not a promise of permanent status.
